content.text: DevScribe is an all-in-one workspace for software engineers, architects, and technical teams.
Create documentation, diagrams, APIs, database queries, JSON payloads, code snippets, terminal commands, and Docker configurations—all in one place.
Instead of switching between multiple tools, keep everything related to a project together and share it as a single collection with your teammates, colleagues, or friends.
The sections below provide a quick overview of each feature along with practical examples and use cases to help you get started.
Engineering knowledge is often scattered across multiple tools:
DevScribe helps you organize all of these artifacts in one place so teams can document, visualize, test, and share technical knowledge more effectively.
A DevScribe workspace is organized using folders and files.
Everything is stored together in a single workspace, making it easy to organize and discover engineering knowledge.
Collections can be shared with teammates, friends, or colleagues, allowing everyone to access the same documentation, diagrams, APIs, queries, scripts, and operational knowledge from one place.
This makes onboarding faster, improves collaboration, and helps teams maintain a single source of truth for their projects.
Create and manage technical documentation using Markdown.
Diagrams can be embedded directly inside documentation pages, allowing architecture, design decisions, and implementation details to live together in a single document.
Test and document APIs without leaving your workspace.
API requests can be embedded directly inside documentation pages, making it easy to explain workflows, provide examples, and keep implementation details alongside project documentation.
Connect to databases and save frequently used queries.
Database queries can be embedded directly inside documentation pages, allowing architecture, APIs, operational procedures, and database access patterns to live together in a single document.
View, format, compare, and validate JSON documents.

JSON documents can be embedded directly inside documentation pages, making it easy to document API responses, Kafka events, configuration files, and data contracts alongside architecture and implementation details.
Write and execute code snippets directly inside your notes.
Code snippets can be embedded directly inside documentation pages, making it easy to explain algorithms, share solutions, and execute code without leaving your notes.

Save and execute terminal commands for future reference.
Terminal commands can be embedded directly inside documentation pages, allowing teams to store frequently used commands alongside architecture, APIs, and operational runbooks.
Integrate your favorite tools directly into DevScribe.
This allows teams to extend DevScribe without changing their existing workflows.
Collections allow you to group related engineering artifacts together.
Collections help keep everything related to a project, service, feature, or system in one place, making it easier to organize and discover engineering knowledge.
Collections can be shared with teammates, colleagues, or friends as a single package.

Instead of sharing separate documents, diagrams, API collections, database queries, scripts, and operational commands across multiple tools, you can share an entire DevScribe collection and give others access to everything they need in one place.
